body:
### Summary

Due to constraints with Gitlab CI we have to perform work in a main working directory which is the checkout of the main project. For our CI we need a sibling repository that we can only check out within the working directory. Both projects have a `pyproject.toml` but build completely independent of each other.

We have to place an (empty) `[tool.uv]` section in the nested checkout's `pyproject.toml` because, otherwise a `uv lock --check` will fail as it inherits `[[tool.uv.dependency-metadata]]` sections that then result in the lock file being considered outdated.

This is especially hard to track down and understand in CI contexts and people running into it spend a lot of time trying to figure out what's going on, as the repos will both build fine independently - they're normally placed next to each other and only forced into the nested shape by the (Gitlab's) CI/CD quirks ... 

### Platform

independent

### Version

0.11 and 0.12 (unchanged until 0.12.23 I assume)

### Python version

independent
title: Implicit inheritance of `uv.tool` section in pyproject.toml across repositories causes confusion between multiple projects in nested checkouts
